nodes.name: Send Discord/Telegram Alert
nodes.notes: ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL can be a Discord channel webhook or, for Telegram, swap this for the Telegram node / bot API sendMessage call. Body shape shown is Discord's; adjust for Telegram.

parameters.content:
## Flow overview

### 1. Webhook
PatchMon sends the trigger to n8n (PatchMon is set up in Part 2 of the series, the webhook in Part 4).

### 2. Exclude vs Security updates only
`EXCLUDED_HOSTNAMES`: Skip entirely and silently
`SECURITY_ONLY_GROUPS`: Security patches only (as per info from Patchmon)

### 3. Resolve
Semaphore lookup returns this host's groups, Proxmox identity, and alert-cooldown state. Semaphore is covered in Part 1 of the series with additional playbooks provided in Part 3 and Part 4.

### 4. Cooldown check
Already alerted on this host in the last 24h, unresolved? Skip silently here, before any template/lock/snapshot/patch work happens.

### 5. Decide
Pick the patch template + lock key from the group→template rule table.

### 6. Security-tier check
Security-only host, but this event is a general (non-security) update? Skip; patch by hand.

### 7. Lock
Run the tag/lock playbook. This runs for *every* host, Proxmox guest or not. It decides internally whether to set a Proxmox API tag or an `mkdir` marker, based on whether `proxmox_vmid` is defined. No database; the tag/marker *is* the lock.
- Locked elsewhere: exit quietly.
- Acquired: continue.

### 8. Open Kuma maintenance window (optional)
Covered in Part 3 of the tutorial. Before anything touches the host. Applies to every host the same way; Kuma doesn't care whether it's a Proxmox guest, only whether any of its monitors are tagged with this hostname.

### 9. Snapshot
Proxmox guests only; skipped entirely for everything else.

### 10. Patch
Run the chosen template, `Limit=<hostname>`, generous poll timeout (up to 45 min; reboots need the room).

### 11. Verify
PatchMon's own still-pending count decides the outcome, 3 ways: success (0 pending), partial (ansible ok but PatchMon still sees pending packages, so Discord warns and Ansible sets a 24h cooldown tag), or failure (ansible error/timeout).

### 12. Alert
Discord/Telegram message for whichever of the 3 outcomes hit.

### 13. Close Kuma maintenance window (optional)
Same gate as step 8; fires on every path out of step 7 onward (success, partial, failure, even a failed snapshot), so a window never gets left open.

### 14. Cleanup
Remove the tag/marker from step 7. This *is* the lock release; nothing else to clean up, there's no separate lock-store.

nodes.name: Start Tag-Add Task
nodes.notes: Runs helpers/patchmon_tag_host.yml -- uses per-site proxmox_api_* from group_vars, so this works regardless of which of your 3 Proxmox clusters the host is on.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ template_id: Number($('Global Config').first().json.SEMAPHORE_TEMPLATE_TAG_HOST), limit: $('Decide Template + Lock Key').first().json.hostname, environment: JSON.stringify({ patchmon_tag_action: 'remove' }) }) }}

nodes.name: Start Tag-Remove Task
nodes.notes: 2026-07-13: now called unconditionally from every alert/success path, since every path that reaches here already passed Lock Acquired?==true and therefore holds a lock (Proxmox tag or local dir) that needs releasing. The old 'Is Proxmox Guest? (Cleanup)' gate was removed as redundant.

nodes.name: Poll Tag-Remove Task
nodes.notes: This pair MUST run on every exit path (success, patch failure, snapshot failure, timeout) to release the lock -- Proxmox tag removal for guests, local lock-dir removal for everyone else.

nodes.name: Lock Busy - Exit
nodes.notes: Another host in this lock group is already being_patched (or this host itself already carries the tag from a prior run). Exit quietly -- PatchMon's next report cycle will re-surface this host later if still needed.

nodes.name: Send Discord/Telegram Success Message
nodes.notes: ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL can be a Discord channel webhook or, for Telegram, swap this for the Telegram node / bot API sendMessage call. Body shape shown is Discord's; adjust for Telegram.

nodes.name: In Alert Cooldown?
nodes.notes: Checked at the very start, before any snapshot/patch/lock work happens. Set by patch_*.yml when a patch run didn't fully resolve pending updates - cleared automatically on the next full success.

nodes.name: Skip - In Alert Cooldown
nodes.notes: Host was already alerted on within the last 24h and hasn't fully resolved yet. Skip silently -- no repeat Discord alert, no repeat snapshot/patch attempt -- until the cooldown tag expires or a human clears it in Proxmox.

nodes.name: Patch Outcome
nodes.notes: 3-way split: success (ansible ok + verified clear), partial (ansible ok but PatchMon still sees pending packages), failure (fallback -- covers ansible error/timeout).

assignments.name: discordMessage

nodes.name: Is Host Excluded?
nodes.notes: Gates everything downstream on Global Config's EXCLUDED_HOSTNAMES list (accepts commas and/or newlines as separators). Checked before the Semaphore lookup even fires, so excluded hosts (e.g. Proxmox host servers) never touch this pipeline at all - no lookup, no snapshot, no patch, no reboot. Patch those manually via the Proxmox UI.

nodes.name: Skip - Host Excluded
nodes.notes: Host is on the EXCLUDED_HOSTNAMES list in Global Config. Exit quietly - no Discord alert, no lookup, no patch attempt. Patch this host manually (Proxmox UI, or SSH + apt directly).

nodes.name: Global Config
nodes.notes:
Community Edition has no native Variables/Environments feature - this node is the substitute. Edit the values above directly. Keep secrets OUT of here (they live in Credentials instead)

EXCLUDED_HOSTNAMES - comma and/or newline separated, case-insensitive, e.g. 'proxmox1,proxmox2,proxmox3'. 

Intended for Proxmox host servers themselves (the hypervisors) or anything else you want to patch by hand only.

SECURITY_ONLY_GROUPS - comma/newline-separated Ansible group names (matched against each host's 'groups' from the lookup, case-insensitive). 

Hosts in one of these groups still get automated, but ONLY on host_security_updates_exceeded webhooks - a host_pending_updates_exceeded (general) webhook for them is skipped silently, patch manually instead. 

UPTIMEKUMA_MAINTENANCE_ENABLED (off by default -- flip to 'true' only once the Semaphore template + vaulted credentials + monitor tags are all in place), 

SEMAPHORE_TEMPLATE_UPTIMEKUMA_MAINTENANCE (blank until you create that template), 

UPTIMEKUMA_DURATION_BUFFER_MINUTES (added on top of POLL_TIMEOUT_MINUTES_PATCH for the Kuma-side auto-expiry safety net).

UPTIMEKUMA_INSTANCES (the non-secret {name,url} list - this is the one place you manage which Kuma servers get called; credentials for each instance live separately in vaulted group_vars.

nodes.name: Standard Update on Security-Only Host?
nodes.notes: 2026-07-13: gates on Global Config's SECURITY_ONLY_GROUPS. True means: this host is in one of those groups AND this webhook is the general host_pending_updates_exceeded event (not the security one) -- skip silently, patch manually. A host_security_updates_exceeded webhook for the same host still proceeds normally.

nodes.name: Skip - Standard Update on Restricted Host
nodes.notes: This host is security-updates-only (Global Config SECURITY_ONLY_GROUPS) and this webhook was a general pending-updates alert, not security. Exit quietly -- patch manually instead.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ template_id: Number($('Global Config').first().json.SEMAPHORE_TEMPLATE_UPTIMEKUMA_MAINTENANCE), limit: $('Decide Template + Lock Key').first().json.hostname, environment: JSON.stringify({ uptimekuma_action: 'start', uptimekuma_duration_minutes: Number($('Global Config').first().json.POLL_TIMEOUT_MINUTES_PATCH) + Number($('Global Config').first().json.UPTIMEKUMA_DURATION_BUFFER_MINUTES || 10), uptimekuma_instances: JSON.parse($('Global Config').first().json.UPTIMEKUMA_INSTANCES || '[]') }) }) }}

nodes.name: Start Maintenance-Start Task
nodes.notes: Runs helpers/uptimekuma_maintenance.yml with uptimekuma_action=start. Duration = POLL_TIMEOUT_MINUTES_PATCH + UPTIMEKUMA_DURATION_BUFFER_MINUTES, so the Kuma-side window can never expire before your own patch-timeout budget does -- and it's the dead-man's-switch if this whole run crashes before reaching the Stop task below.

nodes.name: Parse Maintenance-Start Result
nodes.notes: Re-spreads Decide Template + Lock Key's full context (hostname, isProxmoxGuest, matchedRule, lockKey, semaphoreTemplateId, groups, ...) same as Parse Tag-Add Result does -- required so 'Is Proxmox Guest?' right after this still has isProxmoxGuest to read.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ template_id: Number($('Global Config').first().json.SEMAPHORE_TEMPLATE_UPTIMEKUMA_MAINTENANCE), limit: $('Decide Template + Lock Key').first().json.hostname, environment: JSON.stringify({ uptimekuma_action: 'stop', uptimekuma_instances: JSON.parse($('Global Config').first().json.UPTIMEKUMA_INSTANCES || '[]') }) }) }}

nodes.name: Start Maintenance-Stop Task
nodes.notes: Runs helpers/uptimekuma_maintenance.yml with uptimekuma_action=stop -- deletes the maintenance window on every instance where one exists for this host. Fires unconditionally on every exit path (success/partial/failure), same as Start Tag-Remove Task right after it. The duration-based auto-expiry on the Start side is the failsafe if this never runs; this is the normal-path cleanup.

parameters.content:
## Before running:

Community Edition has no native Variables/Environments panel (paid-plan feature) -- config lives in the **Global Config** node instead. Fill in your values. If your Semaphore instance is not allowing parallel tasks, then if you have more hosts to be patched, they will be queued and this will impact the polling times - **ensure you give all jobs generous timeout**.

**Credentials to create (Credentials store, not Global Config):** Semaphore API Token (HTTP Bearer Auth).

**Semaphore Task Templates needed:** PatchMon Inventory Lookup (patchmon_lookup.yml), plus existing Snapshot/Debian/Nginx/Galera templates from Part 1.

**Import order:** import the sub-workflow "PatchMon - Poll Semaphore Sub-Task" FIRST, then this one. Open each "Poll ... Task" Execute Workflow node here and pick it from the list (workflowId cannot be pre-wired across separate imports). There are several tiles to check this for (whenver the sub-workflow is called).

conditions.leftValue: ={{ (String($('Global Config').first().json.UPTIMEKUMA_MAINTENANCE_ENABLED || '')).toLowerCase() === 'true' && (() => { try { return JSON.parse($('Global Config').first().json.UPTIMEKUMA_INSTANCES || '[]').length > 0; } catch (e) { return false; } })() && !!(($('Global Config').first().json.SEMAPHORE_TEMPLATE_UPTIMEKUMA_MAINTENANCE || '').trim()) }}

nodes.name: Kuma Maintenance Enabled? (Stop)
nodes.notes: OPTIONAL FEATURE, OFF BY DEFAULT. True only when Global Config's UPTIMEKUMA_MAINTENANCE_ENABLED='true' AND UPTIMEKUMA_INSTANCES has at least one entry AND SEMAPHORE_TEMPLATE_UPTIMEKUMA_MAINTENANCE is set. Until you set all three, this always routes 'false' -- patching behaves exactly as it did before this feature existed.

Until you set all three, this always routes 'false' -- patching behaves exactly as it did before this feature existed.
